_doc: Daily Viral Picks scan settings (owner request 2026-10-04; Instagram + TikTok viral only, owner 2026-10-05). Used by /daily-run. vidIQ tool: vidiq_instagram_tiktok_outlier_search (5 credits a call, whatever resultsPerPlatform is), ONE call each weekday (budget.scan_days), Biscuit and Reginald in turn, each rotating through its own themes. Dates are relative: posted_within_days -> datePostedAfter = today - N days. `defaults` holds only vidIQ parameters; already-seen videos are excluded by the skill (excludeContentIds = `bin/studio fav seen`, at most 100 ids).

budget._note: One Instagram + TikTok outlier search each weekday (5 credits a call) = 25 a week, about 108 a month of the 150-credit plan. No watches: `breakdowns_per_week` and `watches_per_character` are 0 because the free local `bin/studio source analyze` of an approved pick's clip replaces the vidIQ breakdown. The search is skipped when vidiq_balance is under `balance_floor` (the run logs `vidiq: skipped, balance N, refills <date>`).

tier_rules._doc: The category (tier) of a pick the analyst did not tier, in this order; the first rule that holds wins. A pick with an explicit proposal.tier keeps it. studio/favorites.py TIER_RULES and terminal/src/lib/scanConfig.ts must equal these numbers (tests pin both). age = days since posted_at (or the scan's age_days); velocity = views per day since posting (the stored proposal.velocity, else views / max(age, velocity_min_age_days)). An unknown age is viral_now.

_saturation_steps: The saturation sub-score from saturation_count (similar outliers found in the last 7 days): the first row whose min_count the count reaches. studio.favorites.saturation_score and the terminal's saturationScore read the same table.

access.name: vidIQ outlier search
access.what: Instagram Reels and TikTok, the only places we scan for viral clips: views, how far the video beats its creator's median (the outlier score), and the hook, format and audio analysis. One search each weekday

access.name: vidIQ watch
access.what: A scene-by-scene breakdown of one short video. Not in the daily plan: the free check of an approved clip (people, camera, best window, beat) replaces it

access.name: Higgsfield Genjutsu galleries
access.what: Trending and New: ready-to-drop-in clips, already clean and trimmed, with previews. Filed only as a backup, on a day the scan could not run or found fewer than 2 usable clips for a character

access.name: YouTube stats
access.what: Only the views and dates of iconic moments, to rank them (free)

access.name: TikTok trending sounds
access.what: What is climbing in the UK and US this week (a sound is never posted without its licence)

access.name: Your own links
access.what: Any TikTok, Instagram Reel or YouTube link you paste, approved on the spot

access.name: Clip fetch
access.what: Only for a pick you approved: the public clip is fetched once for the Drop-in, checked here for free, and deleted after posting

video_requirements: One clear performer or animal as the star
No watermark and no other creator's handle
No text burned into the picture
People in the background are fine
A clean 6-9 second window to use (16 at most)
Music: the clip's original audio by default

biscuit.audienceQuery: Culture/Region: US/UK English-speaking; Global: true; Demographics: dog lovers and Gen Z/millennials 16-40 who watch cute pet and dance content;

rotation.query: clothed animal standing upright doing a skilled trend dance, seamless loop, music only
small dog front and centre leading human backup dancers in a trending dance
small dog in an outfit stares into the camera, then hits every beat of a high-energy track
pet with a human job or an ego caption doing a viral trend

fit_rules: one animal or one dancer as the star; people in the background are fine (other_people is recorded, not a gate); a second dancing star is still filed with needs multi_body and held until the multi-body test passes
upright/biped motion for the biped master; four-legged head-bob for the quadruped master
fits Biscuit's traits card (energy, comedy, moves, settings, props: `bin/studio seed status` > traits): bouncy, puppy-cute, a wholesome ego, never clumsy, no voice

reginald.audienceQuery: Culture/Region: UK/US English-speaking; Global: true; Demographics: Gen Z and millennials 16-34 who watch comedy, memes and dance trends;

rotation.query: stone-faced person in a work uniform performs a trend dance perfectly at work, then calmly resumes the task
on-screen premise like 'first day as' then a mundane task done with total seriousness, then the beat drops into a dance
deadpan costumed character, one repeatable action, changing locations
older or formally dressed person steps in and out-dances young people

fit_rules: one performer as the star; people in the background are fine (other_people is recorded, not a gate); a second dancing star is still filed with needs multi_body and held until the multi-body test passes
deadpan-compatible (the joke must survive a straight face)
no real-person likeness, masks or impersonations as the joke
fits Reginald's traits card (energy, comedy, moves, settings, props: `bin/studio seed status` > traits): calm, deadpan, a straight face under absurdity, never smiling, the quiff never moves

outsider.audienceQuery: Culture/Region: UK/US English-speaking; Global: true; Demographics: millennials and Gen Z 18-40 who watch character comedy and history content;

rotation.theme: stranger baffled by a modern object
rotation.query: naive confident character from another era baffled by a modern everyday object
openly AI recurring character talks to a handheld camera, numbered episode
over-formal verbose speaker reacts to modern slang

_themes: Each rotation entry has a `theme`: a short label (at most 60 characters) naming what the entry looks for. A filed pick carries `proposal.theme` = the theme of the entry it matched, or the closest theme of its character when it came from the Genjutsu gallery or the owner. The terminal groups a character's picks by category or by theme.
free_sources_daily: Higgsfield Genjutsu Trending + New galleries (get_presets source=genjutsu): backup picks only, when the scan could not run or found fewer than 2 usable clips for a character that day
TikTok trending commercial sounds (tiktok_music_trending, country GB and US, 7DAY)
YouTube stats of iconic moments only (views and dates; free)
global_reject_rules: a real person's likeness or an impersonation as the joke (the real star is always replaced by our character; a famous clip, meme or dance is fine)
trend more than 7 days past its peak, unless it is an iconic evergreen moment (tier iconic)
sexualised content, or a child as the star or main subject (a Drop-in source shows no child at all)
pick_card_fields: velocity (views per day, worked out at filing)
engagement {likes, comments, shares, saves} when vidIQ returns it
trait_matches (1-4 phrases of the traits card)
analysis (the clip check, after the clip is fetched or attached)
